title: Brazil's Supreme Court converts more than 10 million appeal pages to text with Victor by May 2021, while Victor's theme classifier is still not in production in August 2021
summary: Victor, the AI project of Brazil's Supreme Court and the University of Brasília, has converted appeals to text since December 2020, with more than 10 million pages processed by May 2021.
account: Victor is a partnership of the Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) and the Universidade de Brasília (UnB). It began at the end of 2017 under Chief Justice Cármen Lúcia. It was designed to read extraordinary appeals and identify the most frequent repercussão geral themes. It has four tasks: converting images to text, splitting documents, classifying the main procedural documents and identifying repercussão geral themes. On 30 August 2018 Cármen Lúcia announced that it was in operation, with tests on 27 themes and a claimed triage precision of 84%. She said that work taking a clerk three hours would take five seconds. On 23 October 2018 Chief Justice Dias Toffoli spoke at a seminar reported by the Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ). He said that it did in five seconds what cost a clerk 40 minutes to an hour, with 85% accuracy. The STF's own status report of 19 August 2021 states that only the optical character recognition (OCR) layer had been implemented. That layer ran from the end of December 2020 for extraordinary appeals and agravos, with more than 10 million pages processed by May 2021. The splitter and the classifier were still being put into production with no set date. The ministers always validate the theme indication. No measured time saving or case outcome was published. Prado and Andrade of the University of Fortaleza concluded in February 2022 that Victor saved considerable time in identifying repercussão geral themes. Their study rests on CNJ and STF secondary data and reports no measurement of its own. In May 2023 the STF said that it still operated Victor for repercussão geral triage of incoming appeals, alongside Rafa. It was then finishing tests of the successor tool VitorIA, which is recorded separately. In October 2023 Valle, Fuentes i Gasó and Ajus credited Victor with efficiency, and they also reported inadequate summaries of decisions. They proposed that case records show when Victor intervened.
purpose: Speed up admissibility analysis of extraordinary appeals by flagging the repercussão geral theme that applies. The OCR layer in production is a precondition for that classification and does not perform it.
system: Victor (STF–UnB artificial-intelligence project: OCR, document splitter, document classifier, repercussão geral theme classifier)
developer: Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) with the Universidade de Brasília (UnB)
deployer: Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), Secretaria de Gestão de Precedentes
taxonomy_note: Only the OCR layer is in production, and the time savings claimed for triage are projections.

ratings.reason: The STF reports that every electronic appeal has been converted to searchable text on the day of receipt since December 2020, more than 10 million pages by May 2021. That is a convenience for staff; no time saving was measured, and the classifier was not in production.
No effect on case backlog or on litigants is documented.

ai_role.statement: By the STF's own account of 19 August 2021, the AI classifier that would flag repercussão geral themes was not in production. The only live component was automatic OCR of incoming appeals, which the STF frames as part of the Victor project. Any theme indication is validated by the ministers. The time savings announced in 2018 (three hours or 40 minutes to five seconds) were forecasts made by chief justices at launch. All cited sources are the deployer's news service (STF) and the CNJ, which the same chief justice presided. No independent evaluation was found.

fields.summary: Victor, the AI project of Brazil's Supreme Court and the University of Brasília, has converted appeals to text since December 2020, with more than 10 million pages processed by May 2021.
fields.account: Victor is a partnership of the Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) and the Universidade de Brasília (UnB). It began at the end of 2017 under Chief Justice Cármen Lúcia. It was designed to read extraordinary appeals and identify the most frequent repercussão geral themes. It has four tasks: converting images to text, splitting documents, classifying the main procedural documents and identifying repercussão geral themes. On 30 August 2018 Cármen Lúcia announced that it was in operation, with tests on 27 themes and a claimed triage precision of 84%. She said that work taking a clerk three hours would take five seconds. On 23 October 2018 Chief Justice Dias Toffoli spoke at a seminar reported by the Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ). He said that it did in five seconds what cost a clerk 40 minutes to an hour, with 85% accuracy. The STF's own status report of 19 August 2021 states that only the optical character recognition (OCR) layer had been implemented. That layer ran from the end of December 2020 for extraordinary appeals and agravos, with more than 10 million pages processed by May 2021. The splitter and the classifier were still being put into production with no set date. The ministers always validate the theme indication. No measured time saving or case outcome was published. Prado and Andrade of the University of Fortaleza concluded in February 2022 that Victor saved considerable time in identifying repercussão geral themes. Their study rests on CNJ and STF secondary data and reports no measurement of its own. In May 2023 the STF said that it still operated Victor for repercussão geral triage of incoming appeals, alongside Rafa. It was then finishing tests of the successor tool VitorIA, which is recorded separately. In October 2023 Valle, Fuentes i Gasó and Ajus credited Victor with efficiency, and they also reported inadequate summaries of decisions. They proposed that case records show when Victor intervened.

value.text: Any eventual theme recommendation required validation by the justices.

provenance.basis: The August 2021 STF account distinguishes the deployed OCR layer from the splitter and classifier that still awaited production. A later 2023 notice describes Victor more broadly. The later general description does not supply a deployment date or validate the earlier classification speed claims.
